name: FoldRocket
author: FoldRocket

sections.description:
FoldRocket turns the default WordPress Media Library into a focused workspace for finding, organizing, and using media faster.

Create unlimited virtual folders and nested subfolders, save reusable Smart Views, filter large libraries, upload files, and work with the same organization inside the native WordPress media picker. Your attachment URLs and files in uploads stay exactly where they are.

Visit FoldRocket | Explore FoldRocket Pro

Features

FoldRocket Free works without an account or license key. Every capability marked – PRO belongs to the separate commercial FoldRocket Pro plugin and requires an active license.

Media library and organization

  • Modern media workspace: Browse attachments in responsive grid and list layouts, search the library, inspect file details, and choose different preview sizes.
  • Upload: Add media directly from the FoldRocket top bar.
  • Virtual folders: Create unlimited folders and nested subfolders without moving files or changing attachment URLs.
  • Folder import: Copy structures and assignments from HappyFiles, FileBird, Real Media Library, and WP Media Folder while leaving the original data untouched.
  • Advanced filters: Filter by MIME type, AI status, missing ALT text, unused or large files, orientation, date, author, and filesystem flags; order by date, title, size, or usage.
  • Smart Views: Save, rename, update, and delete reusable filter shortcuts that update with the library.
  • Folder colors: Color-code projects and clients so folders are easier to recognize.
  • Bulk actions: Select multiple attachments to assign them to a folder, download them, or delete them with confirmation.
  • Download ZIP: Package the current folder, Smart View, or selected media in a background job with progress and cancellation.
  • Native media modal: Use FoldRocket folders and search while selecting media inside posts, pages, products, and builders.
  • Bricks media browser: Browse the same virtual folders inside the Bricks media picker.
  • Manual folder ordering: Drag attachments within a folder to keep a custom project-specific order.
  • Localized interface: Use the FoldRocket admin interface in English, Italian, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese (Portugal and Brazil), Polish, Russian, Danish, or Dutch.

View the animated folders demo

AI and metadata

AI features use your own provider key. The site administrator chooses the provider and model, and every generated result can be reviewed before it is applied.

  • AI image analysis – PRO: Analyze images with a BYOK vision provider to produce useful descriptions and tags.
  • AI metadata generation – PRO: Generate title, ALT text, caption, description, and tags, then edit each suggestion before saving.
  • Bulk ALT generation – PRO: Generate ALT text for multiple attachments in a background job with progress, review states, and a final recap.
  • Multilingual metadata – PRO: Maintain per-locale attachment metadata from the Inspector.
  • AI rename on upload – PRO: Optionally turn AI vision results into descriptive, SEO-friendly filenames while preserving references.
  • Edit with AI – PRO: Describe an image change, iterate on the result, compare the preview, and replace the attachment only after approval.
  • BYOK provider control – PRO: Configure supported AI providers and models with server-side API key storage.

View provider setup | View metadata generation | View AI image editing

Cleanup and library insights

  • Duplicate detection – PRO: Scan for exact and near-duplicate media using hashes and visual evidence.
  • Unused media – PRO: Find attachments with no known references without deleting anything automatically.
  • Usage and references – PRO: See where media appears across posts, metadata, featured images, and supported builders.
  • Library health – PRO: Review health scores and a prioritized overview of media issues.

View the duplicate review demo

Image and video tools

  • Image optimization – PRO: Compress images with a preview and keep a restorable original.
  • Crop and rotate – PRO: Apply non-destructive crops or rotations and regenerate WordPress thumbnails.
  • Resize – PRO: Resize an image to exact dimensions with backup and thumbnail regeneration.
  • Format conversion – PRO: Convert between JPEG, PNG, WebP, and AVIF when the server supports it.
  • Remove background – PRO: Remove an image background locally in the browser and save a transparent PNG.
  • Replace file – PRO: Replace an attachment file while keeping the same WordPress attachment ID and references.
  • Rename file – PRO: Rename the physical file safely, regenerate image sizes, and update known URL references.
  • Video optimizer – PRO: Optimize, resize, and convert WordPress video attachments with FFmpeg while retaining a restorable original.
  • Video poster – PRO: Select a frame from the video timeline and save it as a new WordPress image attachment.

Administration and control

  • Feature controls: Enable or disable every entitled capability from the FoldRocket Features page.
  • Background jobs: Run indexing, downloads, scans, and bulk work as resumable jobs instead of blocking the browser.
  • System status – PRO: Check environment details, PHP limits, and plugin diagnostics.
  • White label – PRO: Replace the FoldRocket logo and WordPress admin menu icon with your own branding.

Safe by design

Folders stay virtual, WordPress attachments remain canonical, heavy work runs in background jobs, and destructive actions require preview or confirmation.

Practical workflows for a cleaner WordPress Media Library

  • Build folders around clients, campaigns, products, or publishing workflows instead of duplicating physical files.
  • Use nested folders for broad-to-specific navigation and folder colors for quick visual recognition.
  • Save frequent filter combinations as Smart Views, such as missing ALT text, large files, recent uploads, or a specific author.
  • Keep custom ordering inside project folders while using date, title, size, or usage ordering elsewhere.
  • Import an existing folder structure before reorganizing a site that already uses FileBird, HappyFiles, Real Media Library, or WP Media Folder.
  • Open FoldRocket folders directly from the native media modal instead of leaving the editor to search the library.
  • Select multiple files to move, download, or delete them through one reviewed bulk action.
  • Check usage references before removing media and review duplicate groups one at a time – PRO.
  • Generate missing ALT text in the background, then review every result before applying it – PRO.
  • Use image backups and previews before optimizing, resizing, converting, replacing, or renaming files – PRO.

PREMIUM COMPATIBILITY

FoldRocket works in WordPress admin and does not replace frontend theme templates. Features marked – PRO require FoldRocket Pro.

Themes

  • Standard WordPress themes: Virtual organization stays in the Media Library and does not change frontend attachment URLs or theme output.
  • Bricks: Use FoldRocket folders directly inside the Bricks media browser.
  • Bricks reference scanning – PRO: Detect media used in Bricks content, headers, footers, global settings, theme styles, classes, components, and global elements.

Plugins

  • WPML: Keep one canonical item per translated attachment family and handle related attachment records consistently.
  • WPML and Polylang multilingual metadata – PRO: Serve and manage locale-specific attachment metadata and ALT text.
  • WooCommerce – PRO: Detect media used as product featured images and gallery images.
  • Advanced Custom Fields and custom fields – PRO: Detect attachment IDs stored in ACF and compatible post-meta fields.
  • FileBird, HappyFiles, Real Media Library, and WP Media Folder: Import virtual folder structures and assignments without moving files.

Page builders and editors

  • WordPress Block Editor: Use FoldRocket folders in the native media modal.
  • Gutenberg reference scanning – PRO: Detect images in Image, Cover, Gallery, Media & Text, and other block attributes.
  • Elementor reference scanning – PRO: Detect attachment references stored in Elementor layout data.
  • Bricks: Browse and assign media through the dedicated FoldRocket folder provider.
  • Builders using the native WordPress media modal: Access FoldRocket folders and search anywhere the standard picker is used.
sections.installation:
1. Install FoldRocket from Plugins > Add New, or upload the foldrocket folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu.
  3. Open Media > FoldRocket.
  4. Complete the setup wizard for language and appearance.
  5. If the site already contains attachments, open Settings > Maintenance and select Index library.
sections.faq:
Does FoldRocket move files inside wp-content/uploads?

No. Folders are virtual and attachment URLs remain unchanged. Moving media between FoldRocket folders does not move the physical file.

Can I import folders from another media library plugin?

Yes. FoldRocket can copy folder structures and assignments from HappyFiles, FileBird, Real Media Library, and WP Media Folder. The source plugin data is left unchanged.

Will my media remain available if I deactivate FoldRocket?

Yes. WordPress attachments and files remain in the standard Media Library. Only FoldRocket’s virtual organization and interface are hidden while the plugin is inactive.

Does the Free plugin require an account or license key?

No. All Free features work without an account, license key, or external service.

Does the Free plugin use AI or send data to an external service?

No. This WordPress.org package does not call AI providers and does not connect to FoldRocket services.

Does FoldRocket delete media automatically?

No. Deletion requires confirmation. Duplicate and unused-media tools in FoldRocket Pro present evidence for review and never remove files automatically.

Where do plugin updates come from?

Updates for this Free package are delivered through the standard WordPress.org update system.

Where can I find the source code?

Human-readable source and build instructions for the compiled Free JavaScript are maintained at https://github.com/FoldRocket/foldrocket.

The PHP source and readable CSS are included directly in the plugin.
sections.changelog:
1.4.33 (2026-11-16)

  • NEW: All media now presents saved Smart Views as visual preview cards with live media thumbnails, names and counts before the main library grid
  • FIX: Saved AI provider API keys can no longer be revealed through the browser or REST and remain server-side only
  • UPDATE: An active Pro license must be deactivated before a different license key can be activated
  • FIX: Settings numeric fields use keyboard-friendly text controls that accept digits only without browser number steppers
  • FIX: Resize preset widths accept values from 1 pixel without forcing partially typed values to 16
  • FIX: Folder and Smart View preview cards render video posters or playable first-frame previews, with file-type fallbacks instead of broken images
  • UPDATE: Direct subfolders use the same visual preview-card layout, including media thumbnails, loading placeholders and a clear empty-folder state
  • UPDATE: The All media view now displays the same title and live item count used by folders and saved Smart Views
  • MINOR: Search and grid/list controls share a consistent height, while the view buttons use a cleaner square borderless treatment

1.4.32 (2026-11-13)

  • NEW: Selected media can be downloaded together from the bulk action bar with live progress, cancellation, and per-attachment permission checks
  • FIX: ZIP download jobs queued from the REST API now start immediately in the asynchronous worker instead of remaining at zero until the next cron tick
  • MINOR: Release packages contain compiled runtime assets without bundling readable admin UI source

1.4.31 (2026-11-11)

  • FIX: Permanent media deletion now resolves the complete WPML attachment family, validates every linked record, removes translations and the source consistently, and clears all related FoldRocket index rows
  • FIX: Incremental usage updates rescan both current and previously indexed attachment references when content is saved, so removing an image from a post is reflected without a full rebuild
  • FIX: UI render and stale module failures now recover safely or show a visible refresh action instead of leaving the FoldRocket workspace blank
  • UPDATE: Grid thumbnails expose WordPress responsive image candidates and view-specific sizes so browsers load sharper previews on high-density displays without always downloading originals
  • UPDATE: Library indexing is differential by default and processes only new, invalidated or modified media, while an explicit full index rebuild remains available in Maintenance
  • UPDATE: Active library indexing progress is displayed once in the top workspace area across all FoldRocket screens

1.4.30 (2026-11-10)

  • FIX: WPML attachment translations no longer appear as duplicate media in the library; each translation group now shows only its original attachment while preserving localized metadata
  • FIX: Full library indexing now applies the same WPML source-attachment scope as the media counter, so translated database records are not counted or processed as separate files
  • FIX: The sticky Inspector tab bar now stays opaque above scrolling content and keeps balanced spacing above and below its labels
  • FIX: The mobile Refresh action is centered consistently with the adjacent Upload action
  • UPDATE: The entire Inspector sidebar now scrolls as one continuous surface while its section tabs remain pinned at the top

1.4.29 (2026-11-07)

  • NEW: Opening a folder now shows its direct subfolders before the media list, with folder colors, item counts and one-click navigation
  • FIX: Drag-and-drop uploads no longer show a duplicate dark progress message while the existing upload toast is active
  • UPDATE: The FoldRocket admin workspace has a refreshed indigo interface with more compact navigation, clearer page hierarchy and polished Library, Inspector, Features and Settings screens
  • MINOR: Empty states, contextual help, tooltips, controls and responsive spacing are more consistent across light and dark themes

1.4.28 (2026-11-07)

  • UPDATE: Every Pro capability is now visible as a clearly locked preview, including navigation, Inspector tools and Edit with AI; commercial implementations are not included in the Free package
  • UPDATE: The product is now FoldRocket across the plugin header, WordPress navigation, onboarding, settings, notices, documentation and all 11 interface languages
  • UPDATE: The plugin slug, text domain, PHP namespace, REST namespace, database prefix, hooks, capabilities, CLI commands, JavaScript bootstrap and CSS prefix now use the FoldRocket and frkt identifiers
  • UPDATE: The Free package installs in the foldrocket directory with foldrocket.php as the main plugin file
  • UPDATE: Free updates are delivered exclusively through the official WordPress.org update system; the commercial updater remains exclusive to Pro
  • FIX: The WordPress.org package uses the React and ReactDOM versions bundled with WordPress and passes the reported Plugin Check packaging, readme and database-query checks

1.4.27 (2026-11-05)

  • NEW: Shift plus the arrow keys extends or contracts the current media selection across grid and list views
  • NEW: The Flags filter identifies attachments whose physical file is missing and refreshes their filesystem status when the filter is opened
  • FIX: Media uploaded through the native WordPress media dialog is automatically added to the FoldRocket index
  • FIX: Grid and list controls keep a stable position when switching views
  • FIX: Smart Views load without repeated listing refreshes and the library no longer reserves an empty first grid cell
  • FIX: The Free package preserves the WordPress media integration bridge so the FoldRocket sidebar appears in the native Media Library and media dialogs
  • FIX: WordPress Plugin Check compatibility is improved through prepared queries, WordPress filesystem APIs, validated request handling and cleaner runtime packages
  • UPDATE: Free and Pro packages share the same release version and packaging checks
  • UPDATE: Index and scan library uses a clearer resumable background workflow with progress, interruption and dismissal states
  • UPDATE: All 11 interface languages now include the complete UI catalog, including sorting and scan progress messages
  • MINOR: Inspector spacing, mobile header controls, sorting controls and the upgrade banner are refined across supported viewports

1.4.26 (2026-11-05)

  • NEW: Native WordPress media selection dialogs show the FoldRocket sidebar with Smart Views, colored folders, hierarchy and live counts
  • NEW: Grid view offers three preview sizes, while grid and list cards show clearer ALT status, file weight, pixel dimensions and aspect ratio
  • FIX: Background jobs use lease fencing, heartbeats, resource locks and bounded retries to prevent duplicate or stale work
  • FIX: FoldRocket bundles its Action Scheduler runtime and keeps a durable WordPress cron fallback
  • FIX: REST operations enforce object-level attachment permissions and safer capability checks
  • FIX: The media sidebar and FoldRocket picker tab load reliably, keep a light skin and preserve native WordPress upload drag and drop
  • FIX: Database migrations verify critical tables, columns and indexes after upgrades
  • FIX: Large folder downloads run in bounded background batches with per-attachment access checks and one-time download tokens
  • UPDATE: Library queries, queue indexes and full-text search are optimized for large media libraries and multisite isolation
  • MINOR: Filter alignment, folder hierarchy spacing, sidebar margins and media-modal layouts are refined

1.4.25 (2026-11-03)

  • NEW: The main FoldRocket navigation can collapse to an icon-only sidebar and remembers the chosen state
  • NEW: The desktop inspector can be resized and remembers its width
  • UPDATE: Inspector previews scale with the original image ratio and keep the complete image visible
  • MINOR: Inspector controls and form spacing are refined across light and dark themes

1.4.24 (2026-11-03)

  • NEW: The native WordPress Media Library adds a FoldRocket sidebar in grid and list views with folder colors, hierarchy and live counts
  • MINOR: The native sidebar uses a bordered, top-aligned layout with improved spacing

1.4.23 (2026-11-02)

  • NEW: Library and WordPress media picker filters support ordering by date, title and indexed file size
  • FIX: Full-library indexing runs in resumable background batches instead of stopping after a partial import
  • FIX: Explicit date ordering inside a folder works independently of its manual drag order
  • UPDATE: Unchanged media reuse hashes and image decoding checks memory before processing originals
  • MINOR: Free and Pro packages share the same release version
